* laya: fp16 residual stream (2x faster, bit-exact encoder) + compiled forward

Root cause of the 2x gap vs laya_mlx: mlx_array_new_float makes a float32
0-d ARRAY, and MLX promotes fp16 operands against it to float32 (Python
scalars keep the operand dtype). The GELU/ReLU constants turned the whole
residual stream fp32 from layer 0's MLP on. scalarLike() builds the
constant in the operand's dtype. Encoder hidden states now match the
reference exactly (max|diff| 0.0000, was 0.113); forward 6.1 -> 4.2 ms.

Also:
- forwardBody takes the five device inputs of DecisionModel.__call__
  (ids, attention_mask, marker_pos, marker_mask, qtype); masks and gather
  indices are built in-graph, so the whole forward is traced once per
  shape by mlx_compile (MLX_SERVE_LAYA_COMPILE=0 falls back to the lazy
  graph). Sequence length padded to a multiple of 16 to bound trace count.
- one mlx_eval per batch (features + action head in-graph).
- LAYA_BENCH=1 latency breakdown test (LAYA_BENCH_GAP_MS for paced calls).
- mlx.zig: mlx_logical_not binding.


* tokenizer: HF BPE byte_fallback encode + ByteFallback decode (Laya, Gemma class)

A character with no vocab entry now becomes its UTF-8 bytes as <0xNN> ids
(`BPE::merge_word` semantics: per unknown character, all byte tokens must
exist, else `unk_token`, fused when `fuse_unk`). Previously such characters
went through the GPT-2 byte-to-unicode table, which produced wrong in-vocab
ids (e.g. "ð" for the lead byte of U+2000B). The `ByteFallback` decoder
turns runs of <0xNN> tokens back into bytes (U+FFFD per byte for an invalid
run) instead of leaking the token strings. Both are parsed from
tokenizer.json (`model.byte_fallback`, `model.fuse_unk`, `model.unk_token`,
`decoder` Sequence/ByteFallback), so Gemma 4 picks them up too.

Steer a running agent turn from the composer (#448) (#497)

* app: steer a running agent turn from the composer

Return while a chat generates queues a steering note; the agent loop ends the turn at its next tool-round boundary and the note starts the next turn as a user message, which replaces the continue nudge, restarts the round cap and keeps the transcript's turn shape. A note typed during a plain reply is sent when it ends; Stop keeps the note for the user. The chat loop and TestServer share the nudge text.

* app: a second steering note joins the first; the row is a faded user bubble

Return while a note waits appends to it with one blank line between. Pause, or Up on an empty composer, takes the note back ahead of the draft with the same join; a turn that ends without reaching a step returns it the same way, also on a tab that was not in front. Only the turn that still owns its ledger slot hands its note on, so a Stop during a tool cannot fire it. The row reads as the message it is about to become: a faded user bubble that scrolls past seven lines, fading the last visible lines and drawing its own knob.

perf: prompt lookup stands in for the MTP chain when output copies its context (#523)

* perf: prompt lookup stands in for the MTP chain when output copies its context

MLX_SERVE_MTP_LOOKUP=1. When the last committed tokens plus t1 occurred
earlier in the prompt or output and the match runs back 8+ tokens, the MTP
round verifies that earlier continuation instead of an MTP chain: up to 7
drafts, or 14 when the match runs back 32+. The gate compares tokens per cost
against the chain it replaces, from EMAs of landed drafts; the draft is sized
to the lookup EMA + 2, or to the cap right after a round that landed every
draft.

Lookup rounds apply the pending history stash (left pending, it grows across
lookup rounds into one oversized head forward) and never feed the EV, depth,
planner, round-cost or live-cost state. The MTP round right after one stays
out of the round-cost table, and every untimed round ends the regime interval:
the regime clock runs from the last observed round, so a skipped round was
billed to the next MTP round (858 ms/token at w4 before the fix).

The cost shape is fitted to served round medians on an M5 Ultra: lookup S=8
29.6 ms, S=9 37.0, S=12 43.0, S=15 47.9, S=16 61.2; an MTP round adds ~0.72 ms
per draft. S=16 is a cliff, hence the cap at 14.

M5 Ultra, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, --mtp --mtp-typical 0.2, against main: 11
agent-style tasks 1.17x, copies 1.31-1.48x, worst task -4%; standard decode,
after-32k decode and concurrency within the round spread or better; GSM8K +
MMLU-Pro 114 vs 112 of 130.

* perf: the lookup gate prices both rounds from the measured round-cost table

The gate compared lookup and MTP rounds with a verify-cost curve fitted on one M5 Ultra and one model. It now reads the MTP round's measured ms from round_cost and prices lookup rounds from a new lookup row that lookup rounds feed. The row is runtime only, so the store format and STORE_VERSION are unchanged. A side with no measurement yet uses the fit, scaled by this machine's measured ms per fit unit; with neither side measured, the gate answers as before.

The first lookup round at each draft count is dropped from the row: warmup compiles MTP widths only, so that round carries a kernel compile. spec-stats prints the lookup row on its own line.

* Lay the Voice pane out around the model that runs it

The model comes first now, with its transfer bar and its residency
toggle beside it, because it decides what everything under it means:
whether there is a voice to clone at all, and how many seconds of
reference it wants. Then the text, the reference clip, Advanced
options, and Generate set apart from the settings it acts on. A model
that cannot clone is not asked for a reference at all, and the same
predicate keeps a hidden clip out of the request.

Dictation is one control rather than a glyph and a line of status
under the editor: it says what it is doing and is the way to stop it.
The reference slot is the well the picture panes already use, split
down the middle into its two ways in, so the rectangle a file can be
dropped on is the rectangle that offers to pick or record one. The
Advanced header keeps one label and one chevron in both states and the
whole row opens and closes it.

On the preview side Play and Stop are one button: pause left the
history shelf lit under a clip that had stopped making sound. A shelf
row keeps its waveform throughout and says it is playing by moving.

* Lay the Music pane out the way the Voice pane reads

The model comes first, with its transfer bar and its residency toggle,
then the mode, the clip it works from, the words, the length, Advanced
options, and Generate set apart from the settings it acts on. Duration
is gone from the source tasks entirely: the clip is the length, and the
Source well now says how long the new track will be, read out of the
clip's own header rather than by loading a hundred megabytes of samples.

Both audio slots are the well the picture panes use, and the well stays
once it holds something: the grey block is how you keep your place in a
long form, so it grows rather than vanishing the moment you use it. The
same is now true of the Voice pane's two filled states, which kept the
old bare rows.

The lyrics box can be dragged taller and keeps its height, its guidance
moved inside it as placeholder text, and the instrumental switch sits
with the label it governs: ticking it takes the box away and leaves the
sentence that says the words are kept. The controls above a text box are
one chip style, the menus beside them included.

Advanced options keeps one label and one chevron in both states and the
whole row opens and closes it. Its controls are packed against each
other and wrap when they run out of room, instead of sitting a grid
column apart, and the boxes are as tall as the pickers beside them. A
tempo picked from the menu now appears in the box while it still has
focus: the box declined every value while focused, to keep the caret
still, and so declined values nobody typed.

On the preview side Play and Stop are one button and the disc bounces
while it plays.

* Put the reference gate in the request, and the resize handle in one place

A reference clip only ever reached a model that can clone a voice because
the pane hid the control. The pane is not the only door: the chat tool
builds its own request from the same saved path, and the service sent
`ref_audio` unconditionally at both of its sites. `clonableReference` is
the one answer now, the way the music service already gates its own
fields, and the test measures that rather than a preset's flag.

The drag handle under a resizable box is one type. The video pane's
prompt handle, which the lyrics one was copied from, had been measuring
its drag in `.local` since it shipped: that space is the handle's own,
it moves as the box grows, and the translation subtracts its own effect,
so the box tracked at half the cursor's speed. Both use `.global` now.
Both also set the cursor rather than pushing it, because the lyrics
handle can be removed while the pointer is inside it and the balancing
pop never arrives.

The length test built its fixture as mono while every source clip is
written as 48 kHz stereo, so dropping the channel count from the
duration would have left it green and told everyone their track was
twice as long. The header reader now also refuses a `fmt ` chunk that
lies about its size and anything that is not PCM. The lyrics height got
the clamp-on-decode test its video twin already had, and a header we
cannot read falls back to saying the track is as long as the clip
instead of saying nothing.

Pause is gone from the player too, not just from the button: nothing
called it any more and the property it served still claimed a paused
clip counts as playing. The filled well aligns leading, so a converting
spinner stops centring itself. Templates is the name of that menu in

The traps found on the way are written down: what `.borderlessButton`

* fix(app): keep the mcp.json and providers.json keys the app does not model

Both files are rewritten whole on a save, and both decode into a model that
declares a fixed set of keys — so a key the app does not know is a key a save
deletes. mcp.json is the one users hand-edit and paste from other MCP hosts
(`alwaysAllow`, `timeout`, another host's `$schema`), and providers.json is read
by the server, which can gain a field the app has not learned yet. The previous
fix for this class modelled two more fields (`headers`, `type`); the mechanism
stayed a whitelist, so the next unknown key repeats it.

Unknown keys are now kept in a new `JSONValue` (a Codable value: these files go
through containers, so `Any` cannot carry them) and written back out again.

Also states why the benchmarks folder keeps the app's pre-rename name: changing
it to match would read as the whole history having been deleted.

AndLoad` fails on `$schema`, `alwaysAllow` and `timeout`, and
`testKeysTheAppDoesNotModelSurviveASave` on `timeout_seconds` and `notes`.

* fix(app): keep the marketplace from dropping unmodelled mcp.json keys

Re-materializing a catalog row rebuilt the entry through the memberwise init,

fix(responses): carry Codex namespace tools through declare, return, history (#479)

* fix(responses): carry Codex namespace tools through declare, return, history

Codex wraps each MCP server as a {"type":"namespace",...} tool group; the
old buildToolsJson skipped type:"namespace" whole, so no MCP member ever
reached the model. Expand members under the measured Codex wire name
(<ns>__<child>, suffixed past a flat or earlier collision), split a
resulting call back to (name, namespace) so the client resolves it by its
declared group, and rewrite an echoed function_call to the name the current
turn actually declares — a suffixed group resolves through the collision
recorded at declaration, so a flat shadow (or two groups sharing one join)
still finds the declared name. A uniquely-named bare child also registers,
so a model that drops the prefix is answered. A function_call_output whose
output is a content-parts array now joins its text parts in order (empty
ones skipped, matching joinedTextParts) instead of reading empty.

Regression tests per direction (expand, split, echo rewrite incl. the
multi-suffix and shared-join collisions, parts join); the null-aliases
path frees every wire name. The namespace round-trip is also asserted
over HTTP, non-streaming and streaming, in tests/test_responses_api.sh.

* fix(responses): alias map owns expanded wire names, closing a taken use-after-free

buildToolsJson registered each expanded wire name in the non-owning `taken`
StringHashMap (deinit frees only the table, not the borrowed keys) but freed the
buffer at the end of each iteration when no alias map was passed, leaving `taken`
holding a dangling key. The next namespaced member's collision lookup then read
the freed slot; when that slot was reused by an equal-length name with a matching
Wyhash fingerprint and bucket, a distinct tool was wrongly suffixed `_N`.

Latent in production: the server always passes the alias map, so the free never
ran; only the null-aliases (test) path hit it.

The alias map now always owns the wire names: a local NamespaceAliases is built
when none is passed, every wire name is put into it, and it is freed once after
`taken` is deinited (defer LIFO keeps the borrowed keys alive for every lookup).
A wire name whose alias put fails is freed by the caller rather than leaked, and
the non-null path is unchanged.

Regression test: a fixed-pool LIFO allocator (the SafeAllocator never reuses a
just-freed slot, so it cannot surface this) plus two children whose joined names
share a length and a Wyhash fingerprint, so a dangling key reads the reused slot
as a false collision. Red on revert, green on the fix. The exact pair depends on
the pinned Zig's hash; re-derive it if a toolchain bump changes the collision.

Ports the multi-column mat-vec idea from the Bonsai Metal work on the
llama.cpp fork: each packed 2-bit word decodes once and serves every
activation row (plain decode, batched decode, MTP verify), so 2..8-row
steps stop paying one full decode per row.

- qmv2: one `msv_qmv2_rows` kernel over M = 1..8, bf16 or f16 activations
  (x read as half2 for f16, float2 for bf16), R rows per simdgroup and G
  simdgroups per threadgroup as template args. Needs biases == -scales.
- `planFor` picks the geometry per GPU generation from kernel sweeps on the
  Bonsai 27B shapes: g13 (M1 Ultra) R4G2; g16 (M4 Pro) R4G2 odd M, R2G8 even;
  g17 (M5 Max) R4G2 at M=1 f16, R4G8/R2G8 above, stock at M=5 and bf16 M=1.
  Unmeasured generations and phones keep the previous dispatch exactly.
- Non-Hadamard ternary packs (Prism Bonsai 1) get the kernel: a load-time
  scan arms `ternary_2bit` only when every matmul weight's biases are
  exactly -scales (an embedding only gathered is exempt; the first
  offending tensor is logged otherwise).
- On measured generations a generic-bias weight of a Hadamard pack keeps
  the bias-aware `qmv` at M=1.

Tests: parity vs f32 truth at every M, geometry, dtype and bias layout;
per-generation routing incl. legacy byte-for-byte; the ternary scan; the
qmatmul wiring (red when the ternary branch is removed).

Rejected after measurement: a fused gate/up/SwiGLU GEMV (bit-exact, ~1% at
M=1 on M1 Ultra, slower at M>=2). The GDN state gather/copy-back removed on
the fork does not exist here.

* perf: qmv2 plans send narrow outputs and M5's non-MLP single rows to stock

Kernel sweeps on the remaining Bonsai shapes: below 2048 output rows (GDN
a/b at 48, attention k/v at 1024) too few threadgroups stream K and stock
is up to 2x faster on M1 Ultra and M5 Max at every width; on M5 Max the
single-row kernel only wins at the MLP width (lm_head 1.06x, 17408 rows)
and loses 3-12% below it. Unmeasured generations keep the legacy dispatch.


* docs: Bonsai ternary kernel CHANGELOG line and the per-chip tuning gotcha

* docs: credit @sudoingX's CUDA small-batch kernels behind the Bonsai ternary GEMV

The multi-row decode-once kernel ports the approach of PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp#218
(CUDA: fast, batch-invariant small-batch PTQ1_0 mat-vec) by @sudoingX, by way of
its Metal port on jasontitus/llama.cpp.

* docs: leave CHANGELOG to the v26.9.6 release PR (#518)

The entry moves to the PR description so it lands in #518's Changes list
instead of a second v26.9.6 header that conflicts with #518 and #531.

* test: tell the ternary route from stock by bias, not by rounding luck

The routing test assumed the kernel and stock round differently on a
random fixture. On M4 Max they came out bit-identical, so the vacuity
guard failed. Biases of +scale make them disagree by construction: the
ternary kernel never reads biases.

perf: prompt lookup is on by default, MLX_SERVE_MTP_LOOKUP=0 turns it off (#533)

Under exact acceptance lookup cannot change output, and the gate falls back to the MTP chain when a lookup round would not pay. The M4 Max and M5 Ultra runs found no task where it loses beyond noise.
fix(logprobs): response_format requests return logprobs (#552)
fix(registry): rescan clears a failed load whose dir is still on disk (#550)

fix: quantized KV keeps the activation dtype, so f16 packs stay f16 under --kv-quant (#553)

The affine KV cache allocated its scale/bias buffers as bf16 and dequantized
to bf16 whatever it was fed. On an f16 pack (Bonsai 2) the first full-attention
layer mixed an f16 query with bf16 K/V, widening the residual stream to f32 for
every later layer; the f16 2-bit GEMVs then declined to stock MLX. --kv-quant 8
decoded 2.6x slower (MTP) at 250 tokens of KV on an M4 Pro.

Scale buffers now take the quantizer's scales dtype and dequantize returns the
scales dtype. bf16 models are unchanged.

brew: update to v26.9.5

v26.9.6 — Every Image Seen - Laya Decisions - Steady Qwen3.8 Agents

### Highlights

- **Qwen3.8 Flash Next reaches up to ~243-300+ tok/s decode and 3,362 tok/s prefill, on an M5 Ultra.** MTP drafts from the conversation itself when the reply copies it, so file rewrites and edits decode 1.3-1.5x faster (on by default, `MLX_SERVE_MTP_LOOKUP=0` turns it off); GDN layers run as one GPU dispatch (a few percent on every Mac, 27B included); Ultra chips verify through the fused MoE kernel (+14%); and M5 Ultra fuses the verify across 2 or more streams (+13% at 4 streams). Peak on M5 Ultra, Flash Next mixed 4-8 bit with `--mtp`: 219 tok/s decode, 227 tok/s across 4 streams, 3,150 tok/s prefill on an 8k prompt. Thanks @STRML MVP of this release! (#517, #519, #523, #533, #534).

- **Laya typed decisions.** `POST /v1/decisions` answers score, yes/no and choice questions about a game or app state with Laya checkpoints (`aac6fef/laya-multilingual-mlx`), and concurrent requests are answered in one pass. Thanks @sbusso (#475, #511).

- **Every image in a conversation reaches the model.** Earlier turns and images returned by tools (pi, Claude Code's Read) are seen where they were sent; before, only the latest turn's images were, so an agent that read three pages saw only the last one. An image already seen is not re-encoded on later turns.

- **Qwen3.8 agents stop going in circles.** Earlier turns' thinking is no longer replayed into the prompt, so long agent sessions use about half the context. The cost is a short pause when you send a new instruction; tool rounds are unaffected. `chat_template_kwargs: {"preserve_thinking": true}` in Model Settings restores the old behaviour.

- **Steer a running agent.** Press Return while an agent chat works to queue a note; the agent picks it up at its next tool round as your next message. Thanks @lojza3d (#497, #537).

- **Redesigned Create panes.** Image, Voice, Music, Video and 3D share one layout with the model first, the Video and 3D panes keep your prompt and files when you switch away, and file pickers open over the window. Thanks @lojza3d (#445, #521).

- **The app is now MLX-Serve.app** and the download is MLX-Serve.dmg. Settings carry over; an app updated in place from 26.9.5 keeps its old folder name until the next update renames it.

### Changes
- Claude Code shows thinking as it streams when tools are on.
- A long prompt that does not fit in memory clears other chats' cache to make room instead of failing. Thanks @celestial-rose.
- Long agent sessions keep their cache when memory is tight (#518), and a short chat no longer pushes out a long one that starts the same way.
- Fixed a crash on a repeated one-token prompt in `/v1/completions`.
- A stop string ends the answer, not the thinking: a match inside the reasoning no longer cuts the reply short (#549).
- `chat_template_kwargs` in a request is honoured, so `{"enable_thinking": false}` turns thinking off.
- Mistral 7B v0.3 and similar models keep newlines and tabs in the prompt.
- App chats and agents resend earlier images every turn (Qwen, LFM2-VL, Muse), and LFM2-VL handles images and agent tool calls correctly.
- Text-only models tell the agent when a tool returned an image they cannot see.
- opencode launchers turn thinking on, and Claude Code launched from the app skips permission prompts.
- A request without tools gets the model's reply exactly as written, like other engines.
- Qwen-Image-2.1 is about 10% faster and can return transparent PNGs. Thanks @mrv777 (#510) and @ChadCSong (#481).
- Bonsai 2 decodes faster, up to 20% with several chats at once, and Bonsai 1 packs get the fast kernel too. Thanks @jasontitus (#530).
- The sidebar shows which chats are working, finished or stopped on an error. Thanks @lojza3d (#536).
- The model browser and Settings no longer freeze while the library rescans. Thanks @LXD-8 (#480).
- Hand edits to `mcp.json`, `providers.json` and the agents list survive a save from the app. Thanks @LXD-8 (#482, #483).
- Codex sees its MCP tools. Thanks @kmahara (#479).
- `mlx-serve pull` downloads everything Kokoro and Qwen3-TTS need to speak. Thanks @brandondyal (#526).
- Very long sessions (250k+ tokens) restore reliably from the SSD cache. Thanks @brandondyal (#527).
- `logprobs` work with `response_format` (JSON mode and JSON schema). Thanks @brandondyal (#552).
- A model that failed to load can be loaded again after its files are fixed, without restarting the server. Thanks @brandondyal (#550).
- The web console has a new icon toolbar, and its media tools can be turned off.
